scope: Provider-neutral adversarial review of source/PIT readiness across the active orthogonal candidate frontier, with emphasis on immutable historical snapshots, public-observation clocks, frozen mappings, revision lineage and overlap/confounding. The current frontier explicitly includes Q202-Q204 information absence, financing transmission, and public-information latency.
prompt: Act as an independent adversarial methods reviewer. Apply the same challenge standard used in the Grok Q194-Q201 review, extended to the Q202-Q204 information-timing family to every source/PIT candidate you inspect. A current live endpoint probe, current documentation page, content hash, HTTP marker or current API response is NOT durable historical evidence. Treat source-feasibility readiness as provisional unless it is bound to an immutable dated snapshot/vintage or another explicitly frozen historical artifact. Attack: (1) current-endpoint drift and retrospective source-readiness changes; (2) historical observation/publication timestamps; (3) revision/amendment/correction/QC/prosecution lineage; (4) frozen pre-event entity/exposure mappings; (5) same-day/date-only leakage; (6) cross-candidate overlap/confounding and convergence; (7) whether synthetic mutation tests remain valid in candidate-specific compilers. For every proposed next step specify the minimal deterministic falsifier and exact missing artifact. Do not rank candidates by returns, inspect returns/holdouts, select assets, tune parameters/thresholds/horizons, change gates, authorize performance, promote, or execute live trading. Preserve disagreement. End with a structured action handoff. The review itself is worker material, never scientific evidence.
